sanskrit.deva:
द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते ।
तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्त्यनश्नन्नन्योऽभिचाकशीति ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pariṣasvajāte |
tayor anyaḥ pippalaṃ svādv atty anaśnann anyo 'bhicākaśīti || 1 ||

lines.iast: dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pariṣasvajāte
lines.deva: द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते

lines.iast: tayor anyaḥ pippalaṃ svādv atty anaśnann anyo 'bhicākaśīti
lines.deva: तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्त्यनश्नन्नन्योऽभिचाकशीति

padaccheda.iast: dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānam vṛkṣam pariṣasvajāte tayoḥ anyaḥ pippalam svādu atti anaśnan anyaḥ abhicākaśīti
padaccheda.deva: द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानम् वृक्षम् परिषस्वजाते तयोः अन्यः पिप्पलम् स्वादु अत्ति अनश्नन् अन्यः अभिचाकशीति

translations.text: Two birds, companions and friends, cling to the same tree. Of the two, one eats the sweet fruit; the other, not eating, looks on.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the muṇḍaka: the higher knowledge has been told, by which the imperishable, true Puruṣa is attained, whose attainment utterly destroys the knot of the heart and the other causes of the round; and the yoga that is the means of seeing it has been told under the figure of taking up the bow and the rest. Now the means that help it, truth and the others, are to be told; and the truth is settled again, chiefly, in another way. Because it is so very hard to fathom, a mantra that is like a sūtra is set down to settle the highest reality, though this has already been done.

Śaṅkara: suparṇā: of beautiful flight, or simply birds. sayujā: always joined together. sakhāyā: of the same name, with the same cause of manifestation. samānaṃ vṛkṣam: one and the same tree, as the seat where both are perceived: the body, called a tree because it is cut down; they cling to it, like two birds to a tree, for the enjoying of its fruit. This is the aśvattha tree with its root above and its branches below, sprung from the root that is the unmanifest, called the field, the seat of the fruits of the actions of all beings. The two that cling to it, like birds, are the self whose adjunct is the subtle body, the seat of the impressions of ignorance, desire and action, and the Lord.

Śaṅkara: of the two, one, the knower of the field, resting on the tree of the subtle body, eats without discernment the fruit produced by action, pleasure and pain, sweet with many varied tastes. The other, the Lord, ever pure, conscious and free by nature, all-knowing, whose adjunct is sattva, does not eat; he impels both the eaten and the eater by his mere being as the eternal witness; not eating, he only looks on, for his impelling is only seeing, like a king's.

sanskrit.deva:
समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नोऽनीशया शोचति मुह्यमानः ।
जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीशमस्य महिमानमिति वीतशोकः ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
samāne vṛkṣe puruṣo nimagno 'nīśayā śocati muhyamānaḥ |
juṣṭaṃ yadā paśyaty anyam īśam asya mahimānam iti vītaśokaḥ || 2 ||

lines.iast: samāne vṛkṣe puruṣo nimagno 'nīśayā śocati muhyamānaḥ
lines.deva: समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नोऽनीशया शोचति मुह्यमानः

lines.iast: juṣṭaṃ yadā paśyaty anyam īśam asya mahimānam iti vītaśokaḥ
lines.deva: जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीशमस्य महिमानमिति वीतशोकः

padaccheda.iast: samāne vṛkṣe puruṣaḥ nimagnaḥ anīśayā śocati muhyamānaḥ juṣṭam yadā paśyati anyam īśam asya mahimānam iti vīta-śokaḥ
padaccheda.deva: समाने वृक्षे पुरुषः निमग्नः अनीशया शोचति मुह्यमानः जुष्टम् यदा पश्यति अन्यम् ईशम् अस्य महिमानम् इति वीत-शोकः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. acc. sg.

translations.text: On the same tree a man (the jīva), sunk (in it), grieves, bewildered by his helplessness. When he sees the other, the Lord, worshipped (by many), and (knows) ‘this greatness is his’, he is freed from grief.

notes: Śaṅkara: on that tree, the body, the enjoyer, the jīva, weighed down by the heavy load of ignorance, desire, the fruits of action, attachment and the rest, sinks like a gourd in the sea: he takes the body for himself, thinking ‘this is I, the son of that man, the grandson of this one, lean, stout, with qualities, without them, happy, unhappy’, and that there is nothing else; he is born and dies, and is joined to and parted from kin and friends. anīśā: helplessness, the wretchedness of ‘I can do nothing; my son is lost, my wife is dead, what is my life to me?’ By it he grieves, bewildered, falling into inner anxiety through many kinds of ill, for want of discernment.

Śaṅkara, on the same: going round in this way through the births of ghost, animal, man and the rest, at some time, by the force of pure dharma gathered over many births, he is shown the path of yoga by some most compassionate one; endowed with non-violence, truth, chastity, the renouncing of all, calm, restraint and the rest, his self collected, he sees, meditating, the other, unlike the self marked by the adjunct of the tree: the Lord, not in the round, beyond hunger and thirst, grief and delusion, age and death, ruler of the whole world, worshipped by the many paths of yoga and by men of rites. ‘I am this Self, the same in all, dwelling in all beings, not the other, bounded by the adjuncts that ignorance has made, which is illusion; and this greatness, the world, is the glory of me, the supreme Lord’: when he so sees, he is freed from the whole ocean of grief: he has done what was to be done.

sanskrit.deva:
यदा पश्यः पश्यते रुक्मवर्णं कर्तारमीशं पुरुषं ब्रह्मयोनिम् ।
तदा विद्वान्पुण्यपापे विधूय निरञ्जनः परमं साम्यमुपैति ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yadā paśyaḥ paśyate rukmavarṇaṃ kartāram īśaṃ puruṣaṃ brahmayonim |
tadā vidvān puṇyapāpe vidhūya nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyam upaiti || 3 ||

lines.iast: yadā paśyaḥ paśyate rukmavarṇaṃ kartāram īśaṃ puruṣaṃ brahmayonim
lines.deva: यदा पश्यः पश्यते रुक्मवर्णं कर्तारमीशं पुरुषं ब्रह्मयोनिम्

lines.iast: tadā vidvān puṇyapāpe vidhūya nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyam upaiti
lines.deva: तदा विद्वान्पुण्यपापे विधूय निरञ्जनः परमं साम्यमुपैति

padaccheda.iast: yadā paśyaḥ paśyate rukma-varṇam kartāram īśam puruṣam brahma-yonim tadā vidvān puṇya-pāpe vidhūya nirañjanaḥ paramam sāmyam upaiti
padaccheda.deva: यदा पश्यः पश्यते रुक्म-वर्णम् कर्तारम् ईशम् पुरुषम् ब्रह्म-योनिम् तदा विद्वान् पुण्य-पापे विधूय निरञ्जनः परमम् साम्यम् उपैति

grammar.en: past active participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: When the seer sees the maker, the Lord, Puruṣa, of golden hue (self-luminous), Brahman the source (of all), then the knower, shaking off merit and demerit, stainless, attains the supreme sameness (that is non-duality).

notes: Śaṅkara: another mantra states the same at more length. paśyaḥ: the seer, the knowing seeker. rukmavarṇa: self-luminous by nature, or with an undying light like that of gold. The maker of the whole world, the Lord, Puruṣa. brahmayoni: Brahman and the source; or the source of the lower Brahman (Brahmā). Then the knower, shaking off, burning away with their root, merit and demerit, the actions that bind, becomes stainless, without taint, free of the afflictions, and attains the supreme, unsurpassed sameness, non-duality; for all sameness within duality falls short of it, so this supreme sameness is non-duality.

sanskrit.deva:
प्राणो ह्येष यः सर्वभूतैर्विभाति विजानन्विद्वान्भवते नातिवादी ।
आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिः क्रियावानेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
prāṇo hy eṣa yaḥ sarvabhūtair vibhāti vijānan vidvān bhavate nātivādī |
ātmakrīḍa ātmaratiḥ kriyāvān eṣa brahmavidāṃ variṣṭhaḥ || 4 ||

lines.iast: prāṇo hy eṣa yaḥ sarvabhūtair vibhāti vijānan vidvān bhavate nātivādī
lines.deva: प्राणो ह्येष यः सर्वभूतैर्विभाति विजानन्विद्वान्भवते नातिवादी

lines.iast: ātmakrīḍa ātmaratiḥ kriyāvān eṣa brahmavidāṃ variṣṭhaḥ
lines.deva: आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिः क्रियावानेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः

padaccheda.iast: prāṇaḥ hi eṣaḥ yaḥ sarva-bhūtaiḥ vibhāti vijānan vidvān bhavate na ativādī ātma-krīḍaḥ ātma-ratiḥ kriyāvān eṣaḥ brahma-vidām variṣṭhaḥ
padaccheda.deva: प्राणः हि एषः यः सर्व-भूतैः विभाति विजानन् विद्वान् भवते न अतिवादी आत्म-क्रीडः आत्म-रतिः क्रियावान् एषः ब्रह्म-विदाम् वरिष्ठः

grammar.en: past active participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: This is prāṇa (the prāṇa of prāṇa), who shines as all beings. Knowing him, the wise man does not speak of anything beyond. Playing in the Self, delighting in the Self, active (in knowledge and meditation): he is the best of the knowers of Brahman.

notes: Śaṅkara: prāṇa: the supreme Lord, the prāṇa of prāṇa, the subject here, who shines variously in all beings, from Brahmā down to a tuft of grass, that is, as their self; the instrumental marks the way he is. ativādin: one whose habit is to speak going beyond all others. One who knows this prāṇa of prāṇa directly as ‘I am this’, not by the mere understanding of a sentence, is not an ativādin: when it is seen that all is the Self and nothing else is, what is there to speak of beyond? He who sees something other speaks going beyond it; this knower sees nothing other than the Self, hears nothing other, knows nothing other.

Śaṅkara: ātmakrīḍa: whose play is in the Self alone, not in wife, sons and the rest; ātmarati: whose delight is in the Self alone. Play needs outward means; delight is mere joy and needs none: that is the difference. kriyāvān: active in knowledge, meditation, dispassion and the like. If the words are read as one compound, ‘one whose action is delight in the Self’, either the bahuvrīhi or the possessive suffix is redundant.

Śaṅkara, on an objection: some take kriyāvān to teach the joining of the agnihotra and other rites with the knowledge of Brahman. That conflicts with the plain words ‘he is the best of the knowers of Brahman’; one active in outward rites cannot be one who plays and delights in the Self; only one who has turned from outward action plays in the Self, for the two are opposed, as darkness and light cannot be in one place together. So the teaching of a joining of knowledge and rites here is idle talk; and the Upaniṣad says ‘give up other words’ (2.2.5) and ‘by the yoga of renunciation’ (3.2.6). The active one here is the renouncer active in knowledge, meditation and the like, who keeps the bounds unbroken; such a one, not speaking beyond, playing and delighting in the Self, active, established in Brahman, is the chief of all the knowers of Brahman.

sanskrit.deva:
सत्येन लभ्यस्तपसा ह्येष आत्मा सम्यग्ज्ञानेन ब्रह्मचर्येण नित्यम् ।
अन्तःशरीरे ज्योतिर्मयो हि शुभ्रो यं पश्यन्ति यतयः क्षीणदोषाः ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
satyena labhyas tapasā hy eṣa ātmā samyagjñānena brahmacaryeṇa nityam |
antaḥśarīre jyotirmayo hi śubhro yaṃ paśyanti yatayaḥ kṣīṇadoṣāḥ || 5 ||

lines.iast: satyena labhyas tapasā hy eṣa ātmā samyagjñānena brahmacaryeṇa nityam
lines.deva: सत्येन लभ्यस्तपसा ह्येष आत्मा सम्यग्ज्ञानेन ब्रह्मचर्येण नित्यम्

lines.iast: antaḥśarīre jyotirmayo hi śubhro yaṃ paśyanti yatayaḥ kṣīṇadoṣāḥ
lines.deva: अन्तःशरीरे ज्योतिर्मयो हि शुभ्रो यं पश्यन्ति यतयः क्षीणदोषाः

padaccheda.iast: satyena labhyaḥ tapasā hi eṣaḥ ātmā samyak-jñānena brahmacaryeṇa nityam antaḥ-śarīre jyotirmayaḥ hi śubhraḥ yam paśyanti yatayaḥ kṣīṇa-doṣāḥ
padaccheda.deva: सत्येन लभ्यः तपसा हि एषः आत्मा सम्यक्-ज्ञानेन ब्रह्मचर्येण नित्यम् अन्तः-शरीरे ज्योतिर्मयः हि शुभ्रः यम् पश्यन्ति यतयः क्षीण-दोषाः

translations.text: This Self is to be gained by truth, by austerity, by right knowledge, by chastity, (practised) always: (the Self) within the body, made of light, pure, whom the renouncers see, their faults destroyed.

notes: Śaṅkara: now truth and the other means that help right knowledge are enjoined for the mendicant, all of them chiefly turning away. satyena: by giving up untruth, false speech. tapasā: by the one-pointing of senses and mind (‘the one-pointedness of mind and senses is the highest austerity’, Mokṣadharma 250.4); this, favourable to the Self by turning toward the seeing of it, is the highest austerity, not the cāndrāyaṇa and the like. samyagjñāna: the seeing of the Self as it is; brahmacarya: abstaining from sexual union. nityam: always; it is to be joined to each, like a lamp set within, ‘always by truth, always by austerity, always by right knowledge’ (so too ‘in whom there is no crookedness, no untruth, no deceit’, Praśna 1.16).

Śaṅkara: where is the Self to be gained by these means? Within the body, in the space of the lotus of the heart, made of light, of golden hue, pure: whom the yatis, renouncers given to striving, see, their faults, anger and the other stains of mind, destroyed. That Self is gained by renouncers through truth and the other means practised always, not by truth and the rest practised now and then. This is said in praise of truth and the other means.

sanskrit.deva:
सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः ।
येनाक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत्सत्यस्य परमं निधानम् ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
satyam eva jayate nānṛtaṃ satyena panthā vitato devayānaḥ |
yenākramanty ṛṣayo hy āptakāmā yatra tat satyasya paramaṃ nidhānam || 6 ||

lines.iast: satyam eva jayate nānṛtaṃ satyena panthā vitato devayānaḥ
lines.deva: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः

lines.iast: yenākramanty ṛṣayo hy āptakāmā yatra tat satyasya paramaṃ nidhānam
lines.deva: येनाक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत्सत्यस्य परमं निधानम्

padaccheda.iast: satyam eva jayate na anṛtam satyena panthāḥ vitataḥ devayānaḥ yena ākramanti ṛṣayaḥ hi āpta-kāmāḥ yatra tat satyasya paramam nidhānam
padaccheda.deva: सत्यम् एव जयते न अनृतम् सत्येन पन्थाः विततः देवयानः येन आक्रमन्ति ऋषयः हि आप्त-कामाः यत्र तत् सत्यस्य परमम् निधानम्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Truth alone wins, not untruth. By truth is laid out the path, the way of the gods, by which the seers, their desires fulfilled, ascend to where that supreme treasure of truth is.

notes: Śaṅkara: satyam: the truthful man wins, not the liar; truth and untruth by themselves, not resting in a person, can neither win nor lose. It is well known in the world that the liar is overcome by the truthful, not the reverse; so truth is a strong means. Scripture too shows that truth is the best of means: by truth, by keeping to speech that tells things as they are, the path called the way of the gods is laid out, spread without a break; by it the seers, men of vision, free of deceit, illusion, guile, egoism, pretence and untruth, their thirst gone, ascend to where that highest reality is, the end to be gained by truth, the best of means, the supreme treasure, stored there as the human goal.

sanskrit.deva:
बृहच्च तद्दिव्यमचिन्त्यरूपं सूक्ष्माच्च तत्सूक्ष्मतरं विभाति ।
दूरात्सुदूरे तदिहान्तिके च पश्यत्स्विहैव निहितं गुहायाम् ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bṛhac ca tad divyam acintyarūpaṃ sūkṣmāc ca tat sūkṣmataraṃ vibhāti |
dūrāt sudūre tad ihāntike ca paśyatsv ihaiva nihitaṃ guhāyām || 7 ||

lines.iast: bṛhac ca tad divyam acintyarūpaṃ sūkṣmāc ca tat sūkṣmataraṃ vibhāti
lines.deva: बृहच्च तद्दिव्यमचिन्त्यरूपं सूक्ष्माच्च तत्सूक्ष्मतरं विभाति

lines.iast: dūrāt sudūre tad ihāntike ca paśyatsv ihaiva nihitaṃ guhāyām
lines.deva: दूरात्सुदूरे तदिहान्तिके च पश्यत्स्विहैव निहितं गुहायाम्

padaccheda.iast: bṛhat ca tat divyam acintya-rūpam sūkṣmāt ca tat sūkṣmataram vibhāti dūrāt sudūre tat iha antike ca paśyatsu iha eva nihitam guhāyām
padaccheda.deva: बृहत् च तत् दिव्यम् अचिन्त्य-रूपम् सूक्ष्मात् च तत् सूक्ष्मतरम् विभाति दूरात् सुदूरे तत् इह अन्तिके च पश्यत्सु इह एव निहितम् गुहायाम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Great is that, self-luminous, of unthinkable form; subtler than the subtle, it shines (in many forms). It is farther than the far, and near, here (in the body); here, in those who see, it is set in the cave (of the intellect).

notes: Śaṅkara: what it is and what its nature: bṛhat: great, this Brahman, the subject, to be gained by truth and the other means, since it pervades all. divyam: self-luminous, beyond the senses; so its form cannot be thought. Subtler than space and the other subtle things, for its subtlety is unsurpassed, being the cause of all. vibhāti: it shines variously in the forms of sun, moon and the rest. It is farther than the far, wholly out of reach of those who do not know; and near, here in the body, being the Self of those who know, and the innermost of all (‘within space’, says scripture). paśyatsu: in conscious beings, it is set, perceived by yogins as the one who sees and the rest; in the cave, the intellect, where the knowers mark it hidden; though it is there, those who do not know, covered by ignorance, do not mark it.

sanskrit.deva:
न चक्षुषा गृह्यते नापि वाचा नान्यैर्देवैस्तपसा कर्मणा वा ।
ज्ञानप्रसादेन विशुद्धसत्त्वस्ततस्तु तं पश्यते निष्कलं ध्यायमानः ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na cakṣuṣā gṛhyate nāpi vācā nānyair devais tapasā karmaṇā vā |
jñānaprasādena viśuddhasattvas tatas tu taṃ paśyate niṣkalaṃ dhyāyamānaḥ || 8 ||

lines.iast: na cakṣuṣā gṛhyate nāpi vācā nānyair devais tapasā karmaṇā vā
lines.deva: न चक्षुषा गृह्यते नापि वाचा नान्यैर्देवैस्तपसा कर्मणा वा

lines.iast: jñānaprasādena viśuddhasattvas tatas tu taṃ paśyate niṣkalaṃ dhyāyamānaḥ
lines.deva: ज्ञानप्रसादेन विशुद्धसत्त्वस्ततस्तु तं पश्यते निष्कलं ध्यायमानः

padaccheda.iast: na cakṣuṣā gṛhyate na api vācā na anyaiḥ devaiḥ tapasā karmaṇā vā jñāna-prasādena viśuddha-sattvaḥ tataḥ tu tam paśyate niṣkalam dhyāyamānaḥ
padaccheda.deva: न चक्षुषा गृह्यते न अपि वाचा न अन्यैः देवैः तपसा कर्मणा वा ज्ञान-प्रसादेन विशुद्ध-सत्त्वः ततः तु तम् पश्यते निष्कलम् ध्यायमानः

translations.text: He is not grasped by the eye, nor by speech, nor by the other senses, nor by austerity or rites. When one is pure in mind by the clearness of knowledge, then, meditating, one sees him, without parts.

notes: Śaṅkara: again the means proper to it alone is told. He is not grasped by the eye, being without form; nor by speech, not being nameable; nor by the other devas, the senses; though austerity is the means to gain all things, he is not grasped by it, nor by Vedic rites, the agnihotra and the rest, however great. jñānaprasāda: knowledge, the knowing of all beings, though by nature able to make the Self known, does not make known the principle of the Self, ever present, while it is unclear and impure, stained by attachment to outward objects and the like, as a mirror covered with dirt or water stirred up. When the stain of attachment born of contact of senses with objects is taken away, and it stands clear, clean and still like a mirror or water, that is the clearness of knowledge. By it one becomes pure in the inner organ, fit to see Brahman; then, meditating with a one-pointed mind, having truth and the other means and having withdrawn the senses, he sees that Self, free of all division of parts.

sanskrit.deva:
एषोऽणुरात्मा चेतसा वेदितव्यो यस्मिन्प्राणः पञ्चधा संविवेश ।
प्राणैश्चित्तं सर्वमोतं प्रजानां यस्मिन्विशुद्धे विभवत्येष आत्मा ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:

prāṇaiś cittaṃ sarvam otaṃ prajānāṃ yasmin viśuddhe vibhavaty eṣa ātmā || 9 ||

lines.iast: eṣo 'ṇur ātmā cetasā veditavyo yasmin prāṇaḥ pañcadhā saṃviveśa
lines.deva: एषोऽणुरात्मा चेतसा वेदितव्यो यस्मिन्प्राणः पञ्चधा संविवेश

lines.iast: prāṇaiś cittaṃ sarvam otaṃ prajānāṃ yasmin viśuddhe vibhavaty eṣa ātmā
lines.deva: प्राणैश्चित्तं सर्वमोतं प्रजानां यस्मिन्विशुद्धे विभवत्येष आत्मा

padaccheda.iast: eṣaḥ aṇuḥ ātmā cetasā veditavyaḥ yasmin prāṇaḥ pañcadhā saṃviveśa prāṇaiḥ cittam sarvam otam prajānām yasmin viśuddhe vibhavati eṣaḥ ātmā
padaccheda.deva: एषः अणुः आत्मा चेतसा वेदितव्यः यस्मिन् प्राणः पञ्चधा संविवेश प्राणैः चित्तम् सर्वम् ओतम् प्रजानाम् यस्मिन् विशुद्धे विभवति एषः आत्मा

translations.text: This subtle Self is to be known by thought (pure knowledge alone), (here in the body) into which prāṇa has entered fivefold. The whole mind of creatures, together with the senses, is pervaded (by him); when it is purified, this Self shines forth.

notes: Śaṅkara: the Self so seen is subtle and to be known by thought, by pure knowledge alone. Where? In the body into which prāṇa, the air, has entered fivefold as prāṇa, apāna and the rest; in that body, in the heart, it is to be known by thought. By what kind of thought: the whole mind, the inner organ, of creatures, together with the senses, is pervaded by him, as milk by butter or wood by fire; for the inner organ of all creatures is known in the world as conscious. In that mind, when it is purified, freed of the afflictions and other stains, this Self shines forth in its own nature, reveals itself.

sanskrit.deva:
यं यं लोकं मनसा संविभाति विशुद्धसत्त्वः कामयते यांश्च कामान् ।
तं तं लोकं जयते तांश्च कामांस्तस्मादात्मज्ञं ह्यर्चयेद्भूतिकामः ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yaṃ yaṃ lokaṃ manasā saṃvibhāti viśuddhasattvaḥ kāmayate yāṃś ca kāmān |
taṃ taṃ lokaṃ jayate tāṃś ca kāmāṃs tasmād ātmajñaṃ hy arcayed bhūtikāmaḥ || 10 ||

lines.iast: yaṃ yaṃ lokaṃ manasā saṃvibhāti viśuddhasattvaḥ kāmayate yāṃś ca kāmān
lines.deva: यं यं लोकं मनसा संविभाति विशुद्धसत्त्वः कामयते यांश्च कामान्

lines.iast: taṃ taṃ lokaṃ jayate tāṃś ca kāmāṃs tasmād ātmajñaṃ hy arcayed bhūtikāmaḥ
lines.deva: तं तं लोकं जयते तांश्च कामांस्तस्मादात्मज्ञं ह्यर्चयेद्भूतिकामः

padaccheda.iast: yam yam lokam manasā saṃvibhāti viśuddha-sattvaḥ kāmayate yān ca kāmān tam tam lokam jayate tān ca kāmān tasmāt ātma-jñam hi arcayet bhūti-kāmaḥ
padaccheda.deva: यम् यम् लोकम् मनसा संविभाति विशुद्ध-सत्त्वः कामयते यान् च कामान् तम् तम् लोकम् जयते तान् च कामान् तस्मात् आत्म-ज्ञम् हि अर्चयेत् भूति-कामः

translations.text: Whatever world the man pure in mind pictures in his mind, and whatever objects he desires, that world he wins, and those objects. Therefore one who wants prosperity should honour the knower of the Self.

notes: Śaṅkara: for one who has realized the Self of all, as described, as his own Self, the fruit is the gaining of all, since he is the Self of all. Whatever world, that of the fathers and the rest, the knower of the Self, his inner organ stainless, his afflictions destroyed, pictures in his mind, ‘may it be for me or for another’, and whatever enjoyments he desires, he gains that world and those enjoyments. Because the knower's resolves come true, one who wants prosperity should honour the knower of the Self, whose inner organ is purified by the knowledge of the Self, by washing his feet, serving him, bowing to him and the like; he is worthy of worship.
